_why_two_files: TWO EXPORTS BECAUSE THEY GATE DIFFERENT BRANCHES, and neither can stand in for the other. `plain` is what every consumer of this engine actually runs today - no entry band, the cap exempting only EQ-backed gaps. `zone` adds the fib ENTRY-BAND exemption, which needs a whole structure + fib engine in the same Pine script and therefore its own harness. The band changes the live gap list on 87.2% of bars here, so a green on one says nothing about the other.
_why_warmup: MEASURED, not guessed: both files match from row 0, so the number is 0. It is never raised to hide a late mismatch - the export starts warm and Python starts cold, so an opening prefix of mismatches is warm-up, while mismatches that RECUR after a clean stretch are real divergence.
_why_provenance: Broker, symbol and timeframe are recorded because a cross-cutting run on 2026-09-01 recorded NEITHER and reproducing it cost three replays - two brokers disagree on the bar count for the same window while both look perfectly healthy.
_exercise_check: A green gate says nothing about a branch neither side entered, so both were MEASURED on this export. Band live on 99.7% of bars; a gap protected by the BAND ALONE (EQ would not have saved it) on 86.2%; the live gap list reaches 29 with the band on against 17 without. The list exceeds the 18 plotted slots on 7.0% of bars (1,413), and on those the whole-array sum columns are the ONLY thing comparing them - without the aggregates this would have been a green covering 93%.
_last_row: compare_fvg.py drops the export's FINAL row: TradingView's last bar is live and unconfirmed, so Pine's `barstate.isconfirmed` detection never ran on it while the CSV carries its current OHLC. Both files red on exactly that one bar until the tool was fixed.
